core_obligations: Reduce to the presentation (proof lines 6152-6160): hypothesis (1) presents the sheafification of G as the amalgamated sum of the sheafifications of E and F over that of D, and hypothesis (2) makes the map from D to F injective after sheafification, so the square is a pushout of sheaves.

Produce the triangle (proof lines 6160-6168): the pushout presentation gives a distinguished triangle of the associated cohomology functors, which is the displayed triangle; functoriality in K follows from the functoriality of the construction.
proof_roadmap: Use hypothesis (2) to see the square as a pushout of sheaves.
Apply the standard triangle attached to a pushout to the section functors.
Read off the displayed triangle and its functoriality.
difficulty_reason: The lemma produces a distinguished triangle relating the cohomology of the four presheaves of a pushout square, under the hypotheses that the sheafification of G is the amalgamated sum of those of E and F over that of D and that the map from D to F is injective after sheafification (statement lines 6125-6150, with the Xy-pic square delivered verbatim). The proof reads the square as a pushout of sheaves using the two hypotheses (proof lines 6152-6160) and applies the standard triangle attached to such a pushout (proof lines 6160-6168), functoriality being inherited from the construction. The non-formal content is the passage from the hypothesis on sheafifications to the pushout statement. The claim is H2: one reduction plus one standard triangle.
